cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine build the job cost and WIP schedule for HANGS Construction.
WIP means work in progress: how far along each job is, and whether it's billed ahead or behind.
Next it sets each contract's value, counting only change orders the owner signed.
Then it ties each job's costs to the ledger and checks them against the job's budget.
One framing bill was charged to the wrong job.
Then percent complete: cost so far, divided by the total expected cost.
One job is now losing money.
Now earned revenue against billings: which jobs are billed ahead, and which behind.
It sets aside the rest of that job's expected loss now, as the rules require.
It proposes three entries, including an adjustment of about $96,000 for over and under billings.
All done. The WIP schedule is ready, with four exceptions for a person, including one job now losing money. Nothing was posted; the controller approves each entry.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
